exclusion_detail: Lead 4k is a 2-step route, but step 1 (Conrad-Limpach synthesis of 4-hydroxyquinoline 2 from ethyl 3-oxobutanoate and 4-methoxyaniline) is given only as 'according to an already-reported protocol [9]' with no procedure in the article (no SI supplied); only the O-alkylation (general procedure 4.2) is described. Reactants of step 1 are named in the text, so the candidate route is transcribed below for reinstatement if the lead allows it.

lead.label: 4k
lead.why: Abstract: 'MIC values as low as 0.3 uM against M. tuberculosis H37Rv'; Results: 3,4-dichlorobenzyl derivative 4k 'showed the highest antimycobacterial activity of the series' (MIC 0.3 uM); also the compound carried into the macrophage study. The abstract itself does not print the label 4k.

reactions.conditions: Conrad-Limpach cyclocondensation 'according to an already-reported protocol [9]'; conditions NOT given in this paper.
reactions.source: Main article section 2 (Results) and 4.2, first sentences

reactions.conditions: General procedure 4.2: alkyl halide (1.2 mmol), 4-hydroxyquinoline (1 mmol), K2CO3 (3.12 mmol), DMF (6 mL), 25 C, 18 h; dilute with water, precipitate centrifuged and washed; 63% for 4k.

notes: Name of 2 is printed only as '4-hydroxyquinoline (2)' (generic); its structure is derived from Conrad-Limpach of ethyl 3-oxobutanoate with 4-methoxyaniline, and agrees with the product names of 3a/4a (6-methoxy-2-methylquinolin-4-yl ethers). The alkylating agent for 4k is not named explicitly: the text says 'benzyl bromides' for series 4 and 'the appropriate alkyl halide', so 3,4-dichlorobenzyl bromide is inferred from the product name (bromide, not chloride, is inferred). Hydroxy tautomer drawn (4-quinolone also possible).
